meta.headline: **Partial implementation (B)** is the dominant outcome: Paraguay reports a concrete on-point measure in the review period across most themes (the SIMORE Plus follow-up system, monetary poverty down from ~26% to ~20%, a universal old-age pension, Inter-American Court land-restitution compliance with 637 Indigenous consultations, judicial digitalisation, 100% school-meals coverage, a new women's prison plus a 2024 alternatives-to-detention protocol, 2025 treaty ratifications, the Indigenous Languages Act, disability-certification reform, online birth registration). **No relevant action (C)** persists on the long-standing asks — a comprehensive anti-discrimination law, a migration law, abortion, criadazgo, the minimum marriage age, the journalist-protection bill — and there are clear regressions (**E**): the 2024 NGO "Garrote" law and Ministry-of-Education restrictions on gender and sexuality education.

blocks.rationale: Act No. 7363/2024 (the 'Garrote' Act), adopted in 2024, imposes vague and disproportionate requirements and penalties on non-profit organisations that restrict freedom of association; the Ombudsman's Office and multiple stakeholders call for its repeal - a regression.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 27 — Several stakeholders (OHCHR summary): "Act No. 7363 (the Garrote Act), adopted in 2024, abusively restricted freedom of association with vague provisions and unclear penalties ... A number of communications recommended repealing Act No. 7363"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 5 — Ombudsman's Office of Paraguay: "Act No. 7363/64 on the Oversight, Transparency and Accountability of Non-profit Organizations ... imposed requirements and procedures that restricted the exercise of the right of association"

recommendations.text: Put an end to legal obstacles to the exercise of freedom of association, in particular in the workplace, and investigate incidents of persecution for trade unionism

themes.theme: Human trafficking & contemporary forms of slavery

blocks.rationale: Paraguay implemented a National Plan to Prevent and Combat Trafficking 2020-2024 (extended to 2025-2026), designated the Ministry of the Interior as lead agency with a dedicated fund (2025), opened the Nasaindy Protection Centre and maintains a specialised prosecution unit; the Committee on Migrant Workers finds standards still unsatisfactory, the ECLJ reports declining case numbers since 2019, and CRC calls for a national anti-trafficking strategy and elimination of criadazgo.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 78 — Paraguay: "The implementation of the National Plan to Prevent and Combat Trafficking in Persons 2020-2024 consolidated the State's response ... It was therefore decided to extend the implementation of the Plan for the period 2025-2026"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 26 — Committee on Migrant Workers: "Paraguay had not yet achieved satisfactory standards in its fight against trafficking in persons and that children, especially those living on the street in the tri-border area, continued to be subjected to exploitation"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 34 — European Centre for Law and Justice: "the number of human trafficking cases that opened every year had decreased since 2019 due to corruption, impunity, lack of resources and inadequate victim support"

recommendations.text: Accelerate the process of effective implementation of the national programme for the prevention of, combating of, and care of victims of, trafficking in persons and the national fund for investment in prevention and the care of victims of trafficking in persons
Step up efforts to combat trafficking in persons, including ensuring the effective investigation of these crimes and accountability for perpetrators
Strengthen its efforts to prevent, combat and punish trafficking in persons, including by providing training for judges, prosecutors, law enforcement officers and immigration agents
Continue addressing trafficking in persons by strengthening enforcement measures, strict punishment and adequate training for judges, prosecutors, law enforcement officers and immigration agents
Further strengthen inter-institutional as well as multisectoral cooperation in the development and implementation of programmes to combat trafficking in persons, especially women and children
Strengthen and intensify the implementation of the national programme and investment fund to prevent, combat, and care for victims of, human trafficking
Step up efforts to prevent, combat and punish trafficking in persons, including by providing training for judges, prosecutors, law enforcement officers and immigration agents

Ensure that human trafficking offences are investigated promptly, thoroughly and impartially, that the persons responsible are prosecuted and punished, and the victims have access to adequate protection and assistance measures, including legal assistance
End high cases of labour and sexual exploitation, and implement a comprehensive victim attention programme

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Safeguard the land tenure systems for all, including indigenous people, and ensure they are protected from all forms of modern slavery, such as forced or compulsory labour and debt bondage

blocks.rationale: The law still allows marriage from age 16 with court authorisation; CRC and UNESCO call for a minimum age of 18 without exception, and reform is only under consideration.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 53 — Committee on the Rights of the Child; UNESCO: "amend the legislation to ensure that the minimum age of marriage was 18 years, without exception"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 143 — Paraguay: "A proposal for regulatory reform to eliminate exceptions to the minimum age for marriage ... is currently under consideration"

recommendations.text: Support, through economic and social policies, the institution of the family and the preservation of family values
Remove all exceptions to the age of marriage

themes.theme: Labour rights and right to work

blocks.rationale: Paraguay adopted a National Employment Plan 2022-2026 and an Integrated Strategy for Employment Formalisation 2025-2028 and is developing National Strategies on Forced Labour and Child Labour 2026-2030; the country team recommends ratifying ILO Convention No. 190, and Indigenous domestic workers report abuse and exploitation.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 28 — Paraguay: "The Integrated Strategy for Employment Formalization 2025-2028 was approved to address the significant challenges posed by informal employment"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 31 — United Nations country team: "recommended ratifying the Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190) ... of the International Labour Organization"

recommendations.text: Protect the fundamental rights of domestic workers in precarious working conditions
Take concrete steps to close the pay gap between men and women, as well as address the underrepresentation of women in public life
Guarantee gender equality, especially by reducing the wage gap between men and women
Ensure labour protection for domestic workers, especially indigenous women
Approve a protocol criminalizing sexual harassment and develop a national action plan to prevent sexual harassment both within and outside of the workplace

blocks.rationale: Monetary poverty fell from about 26 per cent to 20 per cent between 2021 and 2024 and Paraguay implements the Naime Poraveta Poverty Reduction Plan 2023-2030, the Tekopora cash-transfer programme and a universal old-age pension (Act No. 7322/2024, 340,203 beneficiaries); CRC and stakeholders report large numbers of children in poverty, sharp rural-urban and Indigenous disparities and high land concentration.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 18 — Paraguay: "Between 2021 and 2024, the monetary poverty rate in Paraguay fell from approximately 26% to 20% of the population, reaching one of the lowest levels ever recorded"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 26 — Paraguay: "Act No. 7322/2024, which establishes the universal pension for older adults ... currently benefits 340,203 people"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 33 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "the large number of children living in poverty and the regional disparities in access to rights"

recommendations.text: Carry out poverty reduction to substantially reduce the poor population, and improve the living standards of the rural population and indigenous peoples
Continue to implement measures aimed at reducing poverty levels in rural areas, particularly for vulnerable groups
Accelerate the implementation of an effective social policy, focusing on early childhood and aimed at ending intergenerational poverty
Follow-up the efforts made to combat extreme poverty

Continue strengthening the policies and programmes within the existing Social Protection System, which should prioritize those who find themselves in conditions of social and economic vulnerability exacerbated by the pandemic

blocks.rationale: Paraguay enacted a universal old-age pension (Act No. 7322/2024) reaching 340,203 people and runs the Tekopora conditional cash-transfer programme for 573,478 people; CRC still recommends expanding child-grant coverage and improving inter-agency coordination.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 26 — Paraguay: "Act No. 7322/2024, which establishes the universal pension for older adults, provides for the granting of a monthly pension of no less than 25% of the current legal minimum wage ... It currently benefits 340,203 people"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 32 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "increase budget allocations for social protection programmes affecting children ... expanding coverage of the child grant programme"

recommendations.text: Strengthen the social security system to effectively protect the rights of vulnerable groups

blocks.rationale: Paraguay's National Development Plan 2050 and the Naime Poraveta Poverty Reduction Plan 2023-2030 guide long-term, people-centred planning with inter-agency monitoring.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 20 — Paraguay: "The National Development Plan 2050 is the State's guiding instrument for long-term planning ... align public policies, investment and State actions with a vision of sustainable, inclusive and people-centred development"

recommendations.text: Approve the updated version of the National Development Plan

blocks.summary: Access to safe water and sanitation
blocks.rationale: The Ombudsman's Office and country team report persistent violations of Indigenous Peoples' rights to drinking water and sanitation and gaps in rural areas; some progress is noted in the Inter-American Court communities.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 12 — Ombudsman's Office of Paraguay: "the persistent violations of Indigenous Peoples' rights to land, drinking water and sanitation"

recommendations.text: Review environmental regulations in the field of industrial agriculture to prevent water pollution and improve the budgetary allocations of the agencies responsible for their effective implementation, thus facilitating the progressive realization of the human rights to safe water and sanitation

blocks.summary: Access to health care; mental health; maternal mortality
blocks.rationale: Paraguay is decentralising services through family and community health teams, doubled public-hospital mammography machines, enacted a mental-health Act (No. 7018/2022) with a 2024-2030 plan, and adopted a Plan to Reduce Maternal, Fetal and Neonatal Mortality 2023-2030; the UN country team and CRPD report continuing quality gaps in rural and Indigenous areas, prolonged institutionalisation without consent, and that Act 7018/2022 keeps a medical model of disability.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 41 — Paraguay: "The enactment of Act No. 7018/2022 initiated the process of reforming mental healthcare"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 64 — United Nations country team: "the enactment of the Mental Health Act and its National Plan 2024-2030. However, it added that serious shortcomings persisted, including the use of prolonged institutionalization without consent"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 36 — United Nations country team: "challenges continued to surround the quality of healthcare, especially in rural areas and Indigenous communities"

recommendations.text: Adopt measures to strengthen the public health system, ensuring the accessibility, availability and quality of health care, especially in rural and remote areas
Continue implementing the programme on family planning as a strategy to reduce child and maternal mortality
Continue its work to ensure widespread accessibility of quality health care, including for indigenous persons and those living in rural areas
Take further steps to improve national health infrastructure, access to emergency obstetric care and midwifery training, especially in rural areas

Implement the commitment made at the Nairobi Summit on the twenty-fifth anniversary of the International Conference on Population and Development to expand the supply of combined oral contraceptive methods, incorporate sexuality education in all formal and non-formal education, and promote prevention programmes to reduce the high rate of adolescent pregnancies
Continue the effective implementation of the National Health Policy strategy for 2015–2030 to ensure universal, comprehensive and equitable access to health services
Strengthen efforts to prevent HIV transmission, especially mother-to-child transmission, and improve the care for persons with HIV without discrimination
Strengthen measures towards the universalization of quality health care, especially for people in vulnerable situations

Implement the commitment made at the Nairobi Summit on the twenty-fifth anniversary of the International Conference on Population and Development to strengthen maternal morbidity and mortality surveillance systems and death registries, by increasing targeted investment in areas of high mortality rates

Take measures to combat the institutionalization and overmedication of persons with mental health conditions and psychosocial disabilities; and fight stigmatization and coercion against them, inter alia by developing human rights-based services grounded in the community and respectful of free and informed consent in line with the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Ensure access to education and health care for indigenous communities

blocks.summary: Sexual and reproductive health; decriminalise abortion
blocks.rationale: Paraguay adopted a National Sexual and Reproductive Health Plan 2024-2030 and a Plan to Reduce Maternal Mortality, but abortion remains criminalised except where life or health is at risk with no clear protocol (4,691 registered abortions in 2024; 19 maternal deaths by June 2025), the Ministry of Education restricts age-appropriate sexuality education (Resolution 933/2023), and CRC recommends decriminalisation and mandatory comprehensive sexuality education.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 40 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "repealing resolution No. 933/2023 of the Ministry of Education and Sciences ... decriminalizing abortion in all circumstances and ensuring access to safe, timely and quality abortion and post-abortion care services"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 39 — Joint Submission 13: "In 2024, the Ministry of Health registered 4,691 abortions and, as of June 2025, 19 women had died. Under current legislation, women were forced to seek clandestine abortions"

National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 44 — Paraguay: "The National Sexual and Reproductive Health Plan 2024-2030 promotes equitable and inclusive policies to improve access to, and the quality of, care"

recommendations.text: Ensure the protection of sexual and reproductive health and rights to all women and girls, including access to health services and contraceptives
Step up measures to reduce child and adolescent pregnancy, including by ensuring access to adequate sexual and reproductive health and education to all throughout the country
Adopt legislative measures to improve protection for the sexual and reproductive rights of women and girls in accordance with international standards

Consider working on legislation to ensure access to adequate sexual and reproductive health, contraception and education services from childhood. In this regard, Argentina offers to share its experiences in the matter
Strengthen the protection of sexual and reproductive rights, including by ensuring access to sexual health services

blocks.summary: Decriminalise abortion and ensure access to safe abortion
blocks.rationale: Abortion remains criminalised except where life or health is at risk, with no clear protocol; CRC recommends decriminalisation in all circumstances, and stakeholders report 19 maternal deaths by June 2025 and women forced into clandestine abortions.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 40 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "decriminalizing abortion in all circumstances and ensuring access to safe, timely and quality abortion and post-abortion care services"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 39 — Joint Submission 13: "as of June 2025, 19 women had died. Under current legislation, women were forced to seek clandestine abortions"

recommendations.text: Legalize abortion in cases of risk to the health of the woman, rape or severe fetal impairment and decriminalize it in all other cases
Expand the grounds for the decriminalization of abortion, particularly in cases of high-risk pregnancies, for girls and adolescents, and when the pregnancy is the product of sexual abuse

Repeal legislation criminalizing women and girls for having an abortion and take measures to allow legal and safe abortions in cases of rape and incest, in cases where the life or health of women and girls is at risk or when the fetus is not viable, as previously recommended

blocks.summary: Repeal restrictions on gender and sexuality education
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: The Ministry of Education adopted Resolution No. 933/2023 and decision No. 29.664 restricting the teaching of gender and age-appropriate sexual and reproductive health information in schools, and bills to ban gender mainstreaming and abolish the Ministry for Women are pending - regressive against recommendations to guarantee comprehensive sexuality education.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 40 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "the prohibition by the Ministry of Education and Science on disseminating age-appropriate information on sexual and reproductive health in educational institutions"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 73 — United Nations country team: "repealing decision No. 29.664 of the Ministry of Education and Science, which prohibited the teaching of topics related to gender theory in schools"

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Undertake measures to prevent a high incidence of early, unintended pregnancy, including comprehensive sexuality education in schools and access to services in support of sexual and reproductive health and rights

blocks.summary: Prevent and address violence against women and femicide
blocks.rationale: Paraguay implements Act No. 5777/2016 on comprehensive protection of women, declared a social emergency on violence against women and children (Act No. 7239/2024), operates the SOS Mujer hotline, shelters, femicide protocols and electronic monitoring, and made training mandatory for civil servants; Amnesty International and the country team report femicide and very high prevalence persist, Act 5777 budgets remain inadequate, and bills to abolish the Ministry for Women and ban gender mainstreaming pose a risk of regression.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 113 — Paraguay: "The State has stepped up its efforts to prevent and combat violence against women and girls by taking measures under Act No. 5777/2016 ... supplemented by Act No. 7239/2024, declaring a social emergency in respect of violence against women, children and adolescents"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 45 — Amnesty International: "78.5% of women experienced gender-based violence ... legislative initiatives such as a bill to ban gender mainstreaming and another to eliminate the Ministry for Women involved a serious risk of regression"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 50 — United Nations country team: "cases of femicide had been observed in Paraguay in previous years and, according to a national survey, the level of violence against women was very high"

recommendations.text: Ensure that all institutions involved in prevention, including education, as well as in combating violence against women, are equipped with adequate financial and human resources to carry out their missions, in line with target 5.2 of the Sustainable Development Goals
Effectively combat violence against women and girls as well as organized crime and human trafficking, and safeguard the rights of women and children
Keep up efforts in the comprehensive protection of women against all forms of violence, through implementation of legislation and national plans that have been adopted in this regard
Step up its efforts to prevent, combat and punish femicides and all acts of violence against women
Effectively combat and investigate femicides and all acts of violence against women and girls
Combat all forms of violence and discrimination against women and girls and promote awareness of gender-based violence and sexual and reproductive health
Continue its efforts in the field of preventing and combating all forms of violence against women, children and other vulnerable groups
Follow up on efforts made to combat violence against women
Ramp up efforts to protect women and children from gender-based violence and abuse, including through national awareness-raising campaigns to address the root cause of the issue
Step up its efforts to prevent, combat and punish all acts of violence against women and girls and ensure relevant offences are investigated properly
Take additional measures, including legislation, to prevent and combat domestic violence against women
Step up efforts to prevent, combat and punish femicides and all acts of violence against women, girls and adolescents, as recommended by the Human Rights Committee
Strengthen its efforts in addressing gender-based violence and providing adequate support and assistance to victims
Strengthen its efforts to prevent, combat and punish all acts of violence against women, girls and adolescents
Step up efforts to prevent, combat and punish femicides and all acts of violence against women, girls and adolescents
Implement a nationwide monitoring system to provide statistics on incidents of gender-based violence, and develop protocols to instruct officials investigating such cases

blocks.summary: Decriminalise abortion and ensure access to safe abortion
blocks.rationale: Abortion remains criminalised except where life or health is at risk, with no clear protocol; CRC recommends decriminalisation in all circumstances, and stakeholders report 19 maternal deaths by June 2025 and women forced into clandestine abortions.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 40 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "decriminalizing abortion in all circumstances and ensuring access to safe, timely and quality abortion and post-abortion care services"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 39 — Joint Submission 13: "as of June 2025, 19 women had died. Under current legislation, women were forced to seek clandestine abortions"

recommendations.text: Take all necessary measures to promote women’s rights and fight against gender-based violence. Guarantee access to sexual and reproductive rights and health, including by decriminalizing abortion

themes.theme: Participation of women in political & public life

blocks.rationale: Paraguay runs training academies and an Observatory for Women's Political Participation, but women held only about 23 per cent of Congress in 2023, the 'democratic parity' bill has not been adopted, and the country team notes women's representation in governance remains limited.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 31 — Joint Submission 12: "women accounted for only 23.2% of members of Congress and recommended the adoption of the bill on democratic parity, in accordance with the Constitution"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 102 — Paraguay: "women accounting for an average of 22.6% of the legislature in 2023 ... the State recognizes that challenges remain"

recommendations.text: Strengthen its commitment to gender equality and women ’ s sexual and reproductive rights through the implementation of the recommendations of the Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women, particularly by raising the necessary relevance of this issue among the public, members of Parliament, the judiciary and public officials

Continue to consolidate the national mechanisms that allow greater participation and equality of women on an equal footing as well as the promotion and protection of the rights and welfare of women and girls
Increase women ’ s participation in political and public life and increase their representation in decision-making positions
Adopt a law on democratic parity to increase women ’ s participation in political life
Continue measures to promote the participation of women and indigenous communities in political and public life
Promote the participation of women and indigenous peoples in public office and political life
Extend the participation of women in political and public life, thus contributing to their empowerment, and ensure the effectiveness of protection against domestic and sexual violence

blocks.rationale: There is no anti-discrimination legislation protecting LGBTIQ+ people, no legal recognition of same-sex civil unions or of self-perceived gender identity, and stakeholders and Amnesty International report rising hate speech and violence with impunity.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 21 — Amnesty International: "impunity for hate speech and the promotion of discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 61 — REPAR+: "the situation of the LGBTQ+ population in Paraguay remained marked by the absence of legislation, by institutional and social discrimination, and the rise of hate speech"

recommendations.text: Step up efforts to increase the participation of women in political and public life and to eradicate all forms of violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression

blocks.rationale: Paraguay expanded the 'Zero Hunger in Schools' meals programme to full national coverage and runs inclusion support centres, but the Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities reports under-investment in inclusive education and persistent segregated special education, and dropout rates remain high among rural, low-income and Indigenous students.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 43 — Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities: "concern at the lack of investment in the right to education of persons with disabilities ... redouble its efforts to end segregated special education"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 42 — Joint Submission 2: "dropout rates remained high among rural and low-income students as a result of poverty, the lack of infrastructure, poor quality education"

National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 22 — Paraguay: "the 'Zero Hunger in Schools' programme ... achieving 100% coverage nationwide and feeding more than 1,050,000 children and adolescents every day"

recommendations.text: Continue efforts aimed at strengthening inclusive education for all children
Consider measures for ensuring access to education
Ensure that children with disabilities have access to inclusive education
Continue its efforts to achieve the National Education Plan in order to improve access to quality education, particularly inclusive vocational training for persons with disabilities
Strengthen efforts to ensure access to quality education for all children, especially for children with disabilities
Develop programmes to promote equal opportunities for access to quality education for indigenous and Afro-Paraguayan children
Continue its efforts to strengthen measures to ensure that girls can have access to education at secondary and higher levels
Take further measures to ensure that girls can access and complete quality education at the secondary and higher levels
Persist with its efforts to address remaining challenges in the education sector

Further enhance the empowerment of women, through its National Equality Plan, to improve the quality of education and skills development with a view to creating more favourable conditions of work for Paraguayan women

blocks.summary: Repeal restrictions on gender and sexuality education
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: The Ministry of Education adopted Resolution No. 933/2023 and decision No. 29.664 restricting the teaching of gender and age-appropriate sexual and reproductive health information in schools, and bills to ban gender mainstreaming and abolish the Ministry for Women are pending - regressive against recommendations to guarantee comprehensive sexuality education.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 40 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "the prohibition by the Ministry of Education and Science on disseminating age-appropriate information on sexual and reproductive health in educational institutions"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 73 — United Nations country team: "repealing decision No. 29.664 of the Ministry of Education and Science, which prohibited the teaching of topics related to gender theory in schools"

recommendations.text: Repeal Ministry of Education and Science resolution No. 29664 prohibiting the teaching of gender equality and resolution No. 1761 prohibiting the use of a guide for teachers on comprehensive sexuality education

Revoke Ministry of Education and Science resolution No. 29664, which prohibits public education materials on gender equality, reproductive rights, sexuality and non-discrimination, and establish gender-responsive comprehensive sexuality education in schools nationwide

themes.theme: Human rights education, trainings & awareness raising

blocks.summary: Implement the National Plan for Human Rights Education
blocks.rationale: The Ombudsman's Office and JS2 report the National Plan for Human Rights Education has been only partially and unevenly implemented, with gaps in budget, infrastructure and teacher training.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 10 — Ombudsman's Office of Paraguay: "effectively implementing the National Plan for Human Rights Education, ensuring that it was allocated the necessary budget"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 43 — Joint Submission 2: "the implementation of the National Plan for Human Rights Education had been partial and uneven"

recommendations.text: Strengthen the implementation of the National Human Rights Education Plan of 2011
Develop a comprehensive national human rights education plan and ensure its full implementation

blocks.rationale: Paraguay strengthened the Ministry for Women's budget, adopted the first Action Plan on Care 2025-2030, introduced gender-budgeting guidance and increased women's access to land titling and rural housing; the country team reports persistent gender norms restricting women's participation and only 13.4 per cent of titled land plots held by women.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 107 — Paraguay: "a preferential interest rate of financing of 0% for women and 4% for men for the purchase of plots of land ... an increase in women's participation: from 35% to 46% in respect of land allocation"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 54 — United Nations country team: "the persistence of gender norms restricted their full participation in the labour market and society ... women owned only 13.4% of plots of land with firm titles"

recommendations.text: Continue with initiatives in furtherance of gender equality
Take efficient measures to remove the obstacles to achieving full equality and eliminate all forms of discrimination in the promotion of equality between men and women
Intensify efforts to eliminate discrimination against women and girls through awareness-raising programmes that are oriented to equality between women and men and women ’ s empowerment

blocks.rationale: Paraguay adopted the first Action Plan on Care 2025-2030, revived the Tripartite Commission on Equal Opportunities and expanded women's access to finance, land and training; women's representation in governance remains limited.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 106 — Paraguay: "The approval of the first Action Plan on Care for 2025-2030 marked a fundamental milestone in the implementation of the National Care Policy"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 55 — United Nations country team: "women's representation in governance spaces remained limited"

recommendations.text: Invest additional efforts to improve the position of women and children in rural areas of the country, especially in terms of employment and participation in public life (for women) and in the field of education

blocks.rationale: Key reforms sought - a comprehensive anti-discrimination law, a rights-compliant migration law, an 18-year minimum marriage age, criminalisation of criadazgo - remain unadopted.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 12 — Special Rapporteur on minority issues; Committee on Migrant Workers: "Paraguay still had not adopted a law against all forms of discrimination, despite the numerous international recommendations"

recommendations.text: Strengthen statistical data collection to help inform appropriate interventions for preventing and combating all forms of violence against women and girls
Assess the need to strengthen the Paraguayan Indigenous Institute

blocks.rationale: There is no anti-discrimination legislation protecting LGBTIQ+ people, no legal recognition of same-sex civil unions or of self-perceived gender identity, and stakeholders and Amnesty International report rising hate speech and violence with impunity.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 21 — Amnesty International: "impunity for hate speech and the promotion of discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 61 — REPAR+: "the situation of the LGBTQ+ population in Paraguay remained marked by the absence of legislation, by institutional and social discrimination, and the rise of hate speech"

recommendations.text: Strengthen appropriate avenues for reporting and effective mechanisms for investigating gender-based violence and attacks on lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons

blocks.rationale: No cluster rule matched and the evidence base contains no specific information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Strengthen the efforts to end all the abuses against children, including child, early and forced marriage, child labour, sexual abuse and trafficking
Intensify efforts to prevent, combat and punish all forms of child labour
Step up efforts to prevent, combat and punish child labour
Address the increase in domestic and school violence and corporal punishment

blocks.rationale: Criadazgo (unpaid domestic child servitude) persists; a 2024 bill to criminalise it was rejected by the National Congress, though the Government plans to resume the legislative process.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 28 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "eliminate the practice of criadazgo (forced child servitude) and provide full protection to children who were victims"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 51 — Joint Submission 6: "the National Congress had rejected a bill aimed at protecting children against criadazgo on the grounds that it was part of Paraguayan culture"

recommendations.text: Step up its efforts against child labour and adopt regulatory instruments and policies for eliminating the practice of criadazgo , including support for the family of origin and the development of awareness-raising campaigns

themes.theme: Rights related to name, identity & nationality

blocks.rationale: Paraguay's Civil Registry runs a single online birth-registration system with hospital offices in 21 locations, but CRPD reports a 30 per cent under-registration rate for births and CRC calls for free immediate registration for all children regardless of parents' immigration status.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 79 — Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities: "the 30 per cent underregistration rate for births ... step up the activities of the 'Right to an Identity' programme"

National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 144 — Paraguay: "the Directorate General of the Civil Registry implements a single register of persons that allows for the online registration of births and facilitates registration through offices established within hospitals"

recommendations.text: Ensure effective procedures of issuance of birth certificates to all newborn children in Paraguay, regardless of the legal status of their parents, as previously recommended
Further increase the percentage of birth-registered children, especially for those in rural areas
Step up its efforts to ensure that all children born in its territory are registered

themes.theme: Right to participate in public affairs & right to vote

blocks.summary: Political participation of women and Indigenous Peoples
blocks.rationale: Women held only about 23 per cent of Congress in 2023 and the 'democratic parity' bill is not adopted; the Human Rights Committee and country team also note very low Indigenous participation in political life and public administration.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 31 — Joint Submission 12: "women accounted for only 23.2% of members of Congress and recommended the adoption of the bill on democratic parity"

National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 148 — Paraguay: "an inter-agency cooperation agreement between the High Court of Electoral Justice and the National Institute of Indigenous Affairs ... to guarantee the effective exercise of the civil and political rights of Indigenous communities"

recommendations.text: Ensure the full and effective participation of indigenous peoples in decision-making processes at all levels of government, especially by ensuring free, prior and informed consent
Establish effective mechanisms that promote and facilitate the participation of indigenous peoples and Afro-Paraguayans in decision-making processes in political and public life
Ensure adequate measures for promoting the meaningful participation of indigenous peoples in all public decision-making processes affecting them

Ensure access to education and health care for all indigenous peoples and promote their participation in public decision-making processes by finalizing and implementing the Indigenous Peoples National Plan

blocks.rationale: Paraguay acquired 3,115 ha for Indigenous communities (2020-2025) and settled three communities under Inter-American Court judgments, but the Special Rapporteur and civil society report inadequate protection of Indigenous lands, stalled restitution and rising forced evictions, and high concentration of agricultural land ownership.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 68 — Special Rapporteur on minority issues: "Indigenous Peoples' lands were not adequately protected, and noted an increase in forced evictions affecting Indigenous Peoples"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 149 — Paraguay: "Between 2020 and 2025, the State acquired 3,115 ha for Indigenous communities"

recommendations.text: Address the ongoing violations of the land rights of indigenous communities
Implement public policies to effectively guarantee the right of access to land and housing for indigenous communities, incorporating international human rights standards
Strengthen measures to ensure property rights and effective access to land for indigenous peoples

themes.theme: Persons with disabilities: protection against exploitation, violence & abuse

blocks.rationale: No cluster rule matched and the evidence base contains no specific information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Strengthen efforts to promote and protect the right of persons with disabilities

themes.theme: Persons with disabilities: definition, general principles

blocks.rationale: The National Action Plan 2015-2030 is being implemented and disability certification digitalised, but CRPD reports the accessibility law is barely implemented, involuntary treatment continues and Act 7018/2022 keeps a medical model of disability.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 41 — Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities: "the persistence of the medical model of disability in Act No. 7018/2022"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 166 — Paraguay: "The disability certification process has been modernized, migrating to a digital system"

recommendations.text: Continue to harmonize national legislation and public policies with the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Continue its efforts aimed at guaranteeing the rights of persons with disabilities (Azerbaijan).

meta.round: Single follow-up round; procedure discontinued with outstanding points folded into the next periodic report.

paragraphs.title: Human rights violations during the dictatorship (1954–1989) and the transition
paragraphs.recommendation: Duly investigate all cases of serious violations during the dictatorship and the transition period and bring those responsible to justice; ensure prompt, fair and full reparation for all victims and families irrespective of when the claim was filed; and accelerate the search for missing persons and identification of remains, with the necessary resources.

limbs.eval: While welcoming the information on cases No. 3154/89 and No. 53/2017 and the search and compensation efforts, the Committee regrets that many requests for compensation have been refused and requests updated figures and information on the pending compensation bill.

paragraphs.title: Pretrial detention and fundamental safeguards
paragraphs.recommendation: Continue reforms to significantly reduce the use of pretrial detention and ensure non-custodial alternatives (bail, electronic monitoring), with pretrial detention exceptional, reasonable and as short as possible, including for adolescents; and ensure all detainees are informed of the reasons and their rights, have access to a lawyer and can contact family from the very outset of detention.

limbs.eval: The Committee welcomes the enactment of Act No. 6350/19 and Supreme Court Resolution No. 1511, the committee on alternative measures and the juvenile restorative-justice work, but regrets the lack of data on impact and on the use of alternatives.

limbs.limb: (b) safeguards from the outset of detention
limbs.eval: While noting the free legal aid provided nationwide and the ongoing training of public defenders and police, the Committee regrets the lack of information on specific steps taken during the reporting period.

paragraphs.title: Independence of the judiciary
paragraphs.recommendation: Strengthen efforts to combat corruption within the judiciary, including awareness-raising among judges, prosecutors and police; eradicate all forms of interference in the judiciary by other branches and investigate, prosecute and punish interference and corruption; and review the laws and operations of the institutions responsible for administering justice and appointing judges and prosecutors to guarantee independence, impartiality, autonomy and transparency.

limbs.eval: While welcoming the measures to fight corruption and promote transparency in the judiciary, the Committee requests information on their impact and regrets the lack of specific information on measures to eradicate interference by other branches of government.
